segments.title: Technical Difficulties & Rennerton Aftermath
segments.notes: Case and Pepito troubleshoot OBS issues after a weekend Cities: Skylines session (Rennerton) that ended in zombie apocalypse; Pepito barks about barfing on electronics.

segments.title: Trump Town Hall Musical Event
segments.notes: Case and Pepito watch and react to a Trump town hall in Pennsylvania that abandoned Q&A for a 39-minute Pavarotti-and-YMCA dance party while attendees fainted from heat; Case calls it 'nauseating' and 'k-hole behavior'.

segments.title: Amongst the Web: Randy Savage, Nazi Boats, Existential Cats & Rodney Dangerfield
segments.notes: Case reviews viewer submissions: Randy Savage Spider-Man set interview, Florida boat rally splash fight, existential cat, trained face-moving man, 'Man Enough' political ad, 1980s CB radio profanity panic, Rodney Dangerfield 'Rappin' Rodney' cartoon, and Canadian Thanksgiving 'Thanks Givner' song.

segments.title: Kick Currency & Twitch VTuber Crackdown
segments.notes: Jeff Ripple reports on Aiden Ross announcing a Kick currency that pays viewers to watch; Chet interrupts on the trigger word 'science'; discussion of Twitch banning VTuber butt content while Kick allows it.

segments.title: Munch & Crum: Fries vs. Chips & The Raid
segments.notes: Munch and Crum debate potato superiority (fries vs. chips), escalate to ass-compliments and ancient magic choking, then raid out as Case heads to a meeting.

characters.name: Case Blackwell
characters.notes: Anchored the broadcast through technical woes, Trump town hall reaction, Amongst the Web, and handed off to Munch & Crum before a meeting.

characters.name: Pepito
characters.notes: executive producer. Managed the cold open, diagnosed the OBS crash as Rennerton fallout, and provided canine commentary throughout the Trump segment.

characters.name: Jeff Ripple
characters.notes: correspondent. Delivered the Kick currency report, got trap-doored by Case, and was interrupted by Chet's science trigger.

characters.name: Chet (Chet Manscape)
characters.notes: science correspondent. Commandeered the Kick segment after the word 'science' was spoken, declared himself 'three times as fast as Beetlejuice,' and proved the future is free.

characters.name: ChetAI
characters.notes: analytical co-host. Referenced as Chet's neural co-host during the science desk interruption.

characters.name: Kendelle
characters.notes: in-studio contributor. Mentioned calling Case during the Trump segment but did not appear on camera.

lore_notes.fact: Claims to have put half of himself in a time capsule to ensure survival to 2028. [43:57]
States human music sounds like 'a terrifying deep voice demon' and is imperceptible to dogs. [45:24]
Asserts he is 'three times as fast as Beetlejuice' and has never lost a foot race to him. [01:21:36]
Aiden Ross announces a 'Kick currency' allowing viewers to earn cashable tokens for watching streams, positioning as 'bits you can cash out.' [01:18:30]
Reported to have banned VTuber butt content (thong-rubbing on Mario Kart) while Kick permits it. [01:24:32]

episode_summary: Barely Informed News opened with post-Rennerton technical recovery before settling into an extended reaction to a Trump Pennsylvania town hall that devolved into a 39-minute Pavarotti-and-Village-People concert while supporters fainted in the heat. The Amongst the Web desk toured Randy Savage's Spider-Man audition, a Florida boat-rally splash fight, an existential cat, a 'Man Enough' political ad, 1980s CB-radio profanity hearings, and Rodney Dangerfield's rapping cartoon. Jeff Ripple reported on Kick's planned viewer-payment currency, triggering Chet's science desk interruption, and Munch & Crum closed the broadcast with a fries-versus-chips debate that ended in ass compliments, ancient magic choking, and a raid.
